B. Is this measure already running in Southwest Finland wellbeing services county (or in the Tyks university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Stereotactic radiotherapy pathway for early cancer in patients who cannot be operated. Every stage I patient who is too frail for surgery is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy (3-8 visits, no anaesthesia) instead of being left without treatment. The treatment exists in every university hospital; what is missing in some counties is the referral rule.
effect_summary_en: In a Dutch national registry study of 4,605 elderly stage I patients, 7 % fewer went untreated after stereotactic radiotherapy became widely available. That fits our 0.8-point assumption only through our own guess that these patients are about 8 % of all lung cancer patients.
supported_en: Annals of Oncology (2012), Netherlands Cancer Registry data: 7 % fewer elderly stage I patients went untreated after stereotactic radiotherapy became available.
not_supported_en: The pages do not show how big the gain would be in Southwest Finland, or what share of all patients are elderly stage I patients.

in_use_summary_en: Tyks gives stereotactic radiotherapy to about 160 patients a year. Varha said in November 2024 that it can be used as first-line treatment for lung cancer instead of surgery. No page shows a rule that refers every stage I patient who cannot be operated on.
missing_en: No page shows a rule that every stage I patient who cannot be operated on is referred for stereotactic radiotherapy.
summary_en: Tyks, the university hospital that treats Varha's patients, gives stereotactic radiotherapy to about 160 patients a year. In November 2024 Varha said it can be used as first-line treatment for lung cancer instead of surgery. Tyks' lung cancer page says radiotherapy can be given if surgery does not suit the patient, but no page shows a rule that refers every patient who cannot be operated on. A 2012 Dutch registry study found 7 % fewer elderly stage I patients went untreated after this treatment became available. That supports the direction of our assumption, but the 0.8-point size depends on our own guess about how many patients are elderly stage I.
unanswered_en: No page shows a referral rule for inoperable stage I patients, or how many of them are left untreated in Southwest Finland.
